key_insight: Quantum impurity solvers could enable more accurate screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials, but quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated.
engineering_relevance: The framework links electrode-interface energetics and conductivity to solid oxide fuel cell and electrolyser performance, then to potential business value.
method: Shortlist materials with DFT and construct correlated impurity models from electrode–electrolyte interfaces.
Use quantum impurity solvers within GW+DMFT or SEET to calculate finite-temperature Green’s functions.
Connect vacancy energetics and transport properties to continuum electrode models and deployment scenarios.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports illustrative logical-qubit counts and scenario-based value estimates, while identifying convergence tests and classical-solver comparisons needed to assess quantum advantage.
watch_item: Complete resource estimates must include thermal-state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated impurity solves—not just qubit counts.
paper_title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
